# Sọ̀rọ̀ Sókè — The People's Yorùbá Dictionary

> A free Yorùbá–English dictionary built from Wiktionary via Kaikki. Search Yorùbá
> or English, in either direction, with or without tone marks and underdots.
> Fully client-side: the dictionary is downloaded once and then runs in the browser.

A Speak Nigeria project. Live at https://yorubadict.com

## How the site is organised

Every word has its own address under `/yo/`: the spelling with tone marks and
underdots removed, then one English word.

    https://yorubadict.com/yo/gba/take
    https://yorubadict.com/yo/ile/home
    https://yorubadict.com/yo/owo/money

Tone is dropped from the address only, never from the page. `gbà` and `gbá` are
different words and both are shown with their tone marks; the English word is
what tells the two addresses apart, which is why several words spelled `gba`
have addresses like /yo/gba/take, /yo/gba/rescue and /yo/gba/hit.

The `/yo/` segment keeps the root free for pages that are not dictionary
entries. Without it the dictionary would occupy 4,343 top-level names and every
future page would have to avoid all of them.

Each address is a real HTML file with the definitions already in it, so nothing
has to be executed to read one. Full list at https://yorubadict.com/sitemap.xml
(7,109 pages).

- `/` — the front page
- `/yo/<spelling>/<word>` — one entry
- `/yo/<spelling>` — the words written that way, where more than one is. 836 of
  these. A spelling written by only one word has no such page.
- `/about`, `/learners`, `/teachers`, `/building-blocks`, `/contribute`,
  `/speak-nigeria` — pages this project wrote itself
- `/yo/ajami/…`, `/yo/ajami-letter/…`, `/yo/tone-mark/…` — Yorùbá written in the
  Arabic script, the Ajami alphabet's own letters, and the tone marks
- Data quality report — in-app panel, source at `/data/validation-report.json`

Addresses do not move. The English word in each one is recorded in
data/url-slugs.json in the source repository rather than recomputed, so a
reworded definition upstream cannot change where a page lives. Where one does
have to change, the old address redirects.

## Reading the data directly

Reading the pages is now usually easier, but the whole dictionary is still one
file if you want it:

- `/data/entries.json` — every entry, keyed by id, each carrying its own `path`
- `/data/search-index.json` — prebuilt Yorùbá tiers and an English inverted index
- `/data/validation-report.json` — a triaged list of problems in the underlying
  Wiktionary data, each with what it would take to fix and a link to the page

## Notes for anyone quoting from this

Yorùbá tone is segmental, not decoration: `gbà` and `gbá` are different words,
and stripping the diacritics from a headword changes what it means. Entries that
share a spelling *and* its tone marks are the same written word with several
senses; those are kept as separate entries and cross-linked.

Some relationships in the source are recorded without saying which sense they
belong to. Where that happens the site says so rather than guessing, and the
data carries a `resolution` field marking the link as ambiguous. Please preserve
that uncertainty rather than presenting a guess as fact.
